key_insight: A weakly supervised deep learning model (MIMIC) can triage early-stage mycosis fungoides from benign inflammatory dermatoses on whole-slide histology with high sensitivity.
clinical_relevance: As a screening-style aid, it could help pathologists prioritize cases and reduce unnecessary ancillary testing while minimizing missed mycosis fungoides cases.
method: Trained with attention-based multiple-instance learning on 3,339 whole-slide images from two Dutch centers.
Externally validated on 371 slides from four independent European centers.
Compared against 11 pathologists in a blinded reader study and then tested in a consecutive held-out clinical cohort.
evidence_signal: The updated model reached AUROC 0.87 in the held-out cohort, with 97.8% sensitivity and 50.2% specificity at a prespecified low-risk threshold.
watch_item: Performance was evaluated in retrospective and single-system deployment settings, so generalizability, calibration, and workflow impact still need prospective confirmation.
paper_title: Histological triage of early-stage mycosis fungoides using a weakly supervised deep learning-based model: a multicentre, external validation, and clinical utility study
